descriptors.concept_name: Nature and Scope of Review Engagements
descriptors.definition: A review is a limited assurance engagement designed to reduce engagement risk to an acceptable level that is higher than in an audit. It evaluates historical financial statements through sufficient and appropriate evidence gathering to enhance user confidence.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike an audit which provides reasonable assurance, a review provides limited assurance with fewer procedures.

descriptors.concept_name: Application of Standards on Review Engagements
descriptors.definition: Standards on Review Engagements govern the performance of review services by practitioners on financial information. These standards form part of engagement standards where quality control is premised on the firm adhering to quality frameworks.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from auditing standards by targeting lower assurance thresholds and procedure volumes.

descriptors.definition: SRE 2400 governs a practitioner's responsibilities when reviewing historical financial statements when they are not the entity's auditor. The practitioner primarily uses inquiry and analytical procedures, supplemented by additional procedures if potential material misstatements are identified.
inclusion: Form and content of the review report
exclusion: Reviews performed by the independent statutory auditor of the entity
nearby_distinctions: Applies specifically when the reviewing practitioner is independent of the recurring annual audit role.

descriptors.concept_name: Objectives and Reporting Obligations under SRE 2400
descriptors.definition: The practitioner aims to obtain limited assurance on whether financial statements are free from material misstatement using inquiries and analytical procedures. If limited assurance cannot be obtained and modification is insufficient, the practitioner must disclaim a conclusion or withdraw.
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on negative form conclusions rather than positive assurance opinions.

descriptors.definition: Practitioners must refuse a review engagement if there is no rational purpose, ethical or independence requirements fail, required information is unavailable or unreliable, or management integrity is doubtful. Engagements intended to satisfy statutory audit requirements lack a rational purpose for review.
exclusion: Engagements with statutory audit mandates requiring full audits
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between appropriate review scenarios and situations where a full audit or compilation is mandated.

descriptors.concept_name: Preconditions for Accepting a Review Engagement
descriptors.definition: Before accepting a review, the practitioner must verify the acceptability of the financial reporting framework and obtain management's agreement on responsibilities. Management must acknowledge responsibility for financial statement preparation, internal controls, and providing unrestricted access to information and personnel.
exclusion: Engagements lacking management commitment to internal controls or record access
nearby_distinctions: Mandates explicit preconditions similar to audits, tailored specifically for review engagements.

descriptors.concept_name: Terms of Engagement and Materiality Framework
descriptors.definition: The practitioner must record agreed terms in an engagement letter prior to performance and evaluate changes when circumstances shift. Materiality for the financial statements as a whole must be determined and applied identically regardless of the lower assurance level.
inclusion: Materiality determination for financial statements as a whole
nearby_distinctions: Maintains the same concept of financial statement materiality as audits despite lower evidence collection.

descriptors.concept_name: Emphasis of Matter and Other Reporting Matters
descriptors.definition: The practitioner uses an Emphasis of Matter paragraph to draw attention to fundamental disclosed items in the financial statements supported by sufficient appropriate evidence. Other matters relevant to understanding the review or practitioner responsibilities are reported under an Other Matter heading.
exclusion: Matters not presented or disclosed in the financial statements placed in Emphasis of Matter
nearby_distinctions: Emphasis of Matter references disclosed financial data, whereas Other Matter addresses external review responsibilities.

descriptors.definition: Review documentation must provide a sufficient record of the work performed to enable an experienced practitioner with no prior connection to understand the procedures, results, and judgments. Documentation must capture the nature, timing, extent of work, review quality control details, and the resolution of inconsistent information.
inclusion: Recording work performer details and dates
exclusion: Undocumented oral discussions without engagement rationale
nearby_distinctions: Mirrors audit documentation stringency by requiring proof of procedure execution and professional judgment.

descriptors.concept_name: Documentation Standards and Overview of Audit versus Review
descriptors.definition: This concept covers documentation retention mandates and sets up the comparative distinction between audits and reviews. Reviews require fewer procedures and lower assurance thresholds compared to extensive audit testing.
inclusion: Cross-comparison of audit and review characteristics
exclusion: Absence of audit-level control testing in reviews
nearby_distinctions: Bridges detailed documentation requirements with structural differences between audit and review modalities.

descriptors.concept_name: Comparative Distinctions Between Audit and Review Engagements
descriptors.definition: Audits provide reasonable assurance using extensive substantive and control testing with a positively worded opinion. Conversely, reviews deliver limited assurance through inquiry and analytical procedures, culminating in a negatively worded conclusion.
inclusion: Contrast between positive and negative reporting language
exclusion: Equating review conclusions with audit opinions
nearby_distinctions: Contrasts the high-assurance, procedure-heavy audit model with the inquiry-focused, low-assurance review model.

descriptors.definition: SRE 2410 governs the professional responsibilities of an independent statutory auditor when reviewing interim financial information for an audit client. Interim information comprises complete or condensed financial sets spanning periods shorter than a full financial year.
inclusion: Quarterly financial reviews by statutory auditors
exclusion: Reviews performed by practitioners independent of the annual audit appointment
nearby_distinctions: Differs from SRE 2400 by specifically applying to the entity's incumbent independent auditor rather than an outside practitioner.
